page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. The instance delivers 64 physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz, configured with one thread per core for dedicated compute execution. System memory measures 256 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB per core to maintain a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The hardware configuration contains zero GPUs and includes no onboard local storage, depending entirely on networked block storage for persistent data. Baseline networking throughput is rated at 133 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-threaded throughput and memory bus capability. In multi-core tests, the instance reached a Geekbench score of 25,794.0 and demonstrated upper-tier results in Clang software compilation (81,827.0) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (677.28 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth tests recorded 480.23 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 236.01 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-core metrics sit within average distribution bands, reflected in a single-core stress-ng rating of 1,706.49 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,889.0. Text generation during large language model inference shows strong throughput on medium (7B) and large (70B) parameter models.

The instance exhibits high capacity for I/O and caching operations, generating 132.0 million Redis SET operations per second and 114.48 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. The omission of local NVMe storage means workloads requiring heavy disk I/O depend on network-attached storage throughput. Given its 64-core ARM density and wide memory bandwidth, the instance is technically matched for distributed database nodes, in-memory caches, continuous integration build clusters, and high-concurrency web serving environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is an ARM-based general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz and 256 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the platform integrates 133 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local instance storage or onboard GPUs. Benchmarks reveal upper-tier multi-threaded scaling and memory performance, including 480.23 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 81,827.0 in Clang software compilation, and 132.0 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core processing ranks near the median across synthetic tests. With its combination of dedicated physical cores, memory throughput, and network capacity, the instance is engineered for distributed in-memory databases, continuous integration build farms, parallel batch processing, and high-throughput web service deployments.
